_schema.description: New Zealand trades-vendor coverage: field service software, lead generation, insurance, payroll and the licensing and safety bodies trades deal with (EWRB, PGDB, LBP and WorkSafe). Profiles focus on New Zealand-specific facts such as registration and licensing, payday filing with Inland Revenue and KiwiSaver.

vendors.name: Fergus
vendors.tagline: Auckland-based job management software for trades, built by a tradesman, from $53 a month
vendors.market_position: Fergus is job management software created by Dan Pollard, a tradesman who built it while running his own trades business, and is based in Eden Terrace, Auckland. It covers quoting, scheduling, job tracking, job phases, time and materials, invoicing and reporting, with iOS and Android apps and Fergus Pay for card payments. Fergus says it is trusted by more than 25,000 tradies and sells Basic and Professional plans, with a custom Enterprise plan for teams over 10 staff.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Fergus says its support is New Zealand-based, by phone (0800 461 219), live chat and email, in your time zone. It imports supplier invoices from NZ merchants including Plumbing World, Mico, Corys, PlaceMakers and ITM, applies 15% GST automatically and syncs to Xero, MYOB or QuickBooks. Its NZ pages do not mention ACC or PAYE handling.
pros: Published monthly prices with no lock-in contract and a 14-day free trial
Supplier invoice import from Plumbing World, Mico, Corys, PlaceMakers and ITM
NZ-based support team in Auckland
Job phases, deposits and progress payments for staged work
cons: GPS tracking, checklists, job phases and purchase orders are on Professional only
Basic support is email and chat only; phone support needs Professional
Pricing page does not say whether prices are per user or include GST
Certificates, SMS and card payments are charged on top
vendors.typical_pricing: Per month, monthly billing, no lock-in: Basic from $53, Professional from $75; Enterprise (10+ staff) custom quote; timesheet users from $26/month; contractor users $4 per user per day; certificates $50-$100/month; SMS $15 per 100; card payments 2.95% + $0.30; 14-day free trial

vendors.name: NextMinute
vendors.tagline: NZ-owned job management software for builders and construction trades, from NZ$199 a month for up to 9 users
vendors.market_position: NextMinute is job management software for builders and construction trades, based in Auckland with an Australian office in Cronulla NSW. It covers lead management, quoting, scheduling, crew timesheets, job invoicing and financial reporting, with two-way sync to Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks. NextMinute says it is trusted by more than 5,000 tradies and industry partners and that every plan includes all features.
vendors.nz_specific_note: NextMinute says it is New Zealand owned and operated, with an Auckland CBD office and Auckland-based support (09 801 6487). NZ prices are in NZD, excluding 15% GST, and include unlimited setup, training and support.
pros: Published NZD prices with all features on every plan
Month to month with no lock-in contract
Setup, training and ongoing support included
Two-way sync with Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks
cons: Lowest plan is priced for 3-9 users, so small crews pay for the full band
Prices exclude GST
Free trial is 10 days, against 14 days at Fergus and Tradify
Built around project-based construction trades rather than service call-outs
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD per month, excluding GST, month to month: Tradie Growth $199 (3-9 users), Tradie Pro $349 (10-14 users), Tradie Max custom (15+ users); all features on all plans; 10-day free trial, no credit card

vendors.name: Tradify (NZ)
vendors.tagline: Job management software for trade businesses, founded in NZ and owned by the UK's Access Group, from NZ$48 per user a month excluding GST
vendors.market_position: Tradify is job management software for trade businesses, founded in New Zealand and bought by the UK's Access Group under a deal announced in October 2024. It covers enquiries, quoting, scheduling, job tracking, timesheets, invoicing and online payments, and syncs with Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks. Pricing is per user per month with no contract, and Tradify says it serves tens of thousands of tradies.
vendors.nz_specific_note: NZ prices are in NZD excluding GST. Tradify lists an office at 81 Union Street, Auckland CBD, NZ 0800 support numbers and free one-on-one training and phone support. Its NZ pages do not claim ACC or PAYE handling.
pros: Published NZD per-user prices, month to month with no contract
14-day free trial with no credit card
Free one-on-one training and phone support from an Auckland office
Syncs with Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks, with Stripe for card payments
cons: Per-user pricing adds up as the team grows
Timesheets, job photos and certificates need Pro; purchase orders and reporting need Plus
Prices exclude GST, and SMS (20c each) and the Instant Website ($19 a month) cost extra
Now owned by an overseas software group rather than independent
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD per user/month, excluding GST: Lite $48, Pro $52, Plus $62; Custom by request; month to month; 14-day free trial; SMS 20c each, Instant Website $19/month

vendors.name: Builderscrack
vendors.tagline: New Zealand job-matching marketplace for homeowners and tradies, owned by Australia's hipages Group
vendors.market_position: Builderscrack is a New Zealand marketplace where homeowners post a job for free and verified tradies contact them to quote. It says it has been trusted by homeowners since 2007, and in September 2026 its homepage showed about 16,000 verified tradies and more than 980,000 jobs posted. Australia's hipages Group, listed on the ASX, bought Builderscrack in a deal of about $11.8 million announced in December 2021.
vendors.nz_specific_note: NZ-only marketplace with a Christchurch-based support team, owned by Australian parent hipages Group. Builderscrack does not publish its tradie fees on its public pages.
pros: Homeowners post jobs for free, so enquiries come to tradies who sign up
Builderscrack says the tradies who contact homeowners are verified, and homeowners see profiles and reviews
Covers building, roofing, plumbing, electrical, painting, landscaping and other trades
Christchurch-based support team
cons: No public pricing for tradies; costs are only visible after signing up
New Zealand only
Homeowners compare the tradies who respond before choosing one
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices for tradies; fees are not published on Builderscrack's site. Posting a job is free for homeowners.

vendors.name: NZI Insurance
vendors.tagline: IAG New Zealand's business insurance brand, sold through insurance brokers
vendors.market_position: NZI is the business and commercial insurance brand of IAG New Zealand, part of Insurance Australia Group (IAG), whose other NZ brands include AMI, State and Lumley. IAG says NZI provides business, rural and personal insurance through brokers, so trade businesses buy NZI cover through an insurance broker rather than directly.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Sold through New Zealand insurance brokers; there is no direct online quote. Cover, limits and premiums for a trade business are set in the broker's quote.
pros: Backed by IAG New Zealand, part of Insurance Australia Group
Broker distribution means advice on cover for your trade
Business, rural and personal cover available through one broker
cons: No direct online quote; you need a broker
No public prices
Product details for trades are set per broker quote
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through insurance brokers; no public prices

vendors.name: Vero Insurance
vendors.tagline: Suncorp-owned NZ insurer with a Tradies Insurance policy sold through brokers and advisers
vendors.market_position: Vero Insurance New Zealand is part of Suncorp New Zealand, which belongs to Australia's Suncorp Group, and sells through insurance brokers, advisers and partners rather than directly. Its Tradies Insurance policy can combine cover for vehicles, tools, stock and equipment, mobile devices, premises, public and product liability and business interruption.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Bought through a New Zealand broker or adviser (Vero has a broker locator on its site), not quoted directly online. Optional extras include licensed building practitioner cover and defective workmanship cover.
pros: Tradies Insurance bundles vehicles, tools, liability and business interruption in one policy
Optional licensed building practitioner and defective workmanship cover
Broker or adviser helps set cover for your trade
cons: No direct online quote; you need a broker or adviser
No public prices
Excesses, limits and exclusions vary by policy and are set in the quote
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through brokers and advisers; no public prices

vendors.name: AMI Business
vendors.tagline: IAG New Zealand's direct insurance brand, with a Tradies Insurance bundle quoted online or by phone
vendors.market_position: AMI is one of IAG New Zealand's brands, alongside NZI, State and Lumley, and sells business insurance directly to small businesses. Its Tradies Insurance bundle combines cover for tools and equipment (up to $10,000, plus up to $5,000 for employees' tools and belongings) with public liability (broadform) up to $2 million. Tradies can get a quote online or by phone.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Quote online or call AMI on 0800 100 200, with monthly or annual payments. Tools are covered for accidental damage anywhere in New Zealand and for theft from a locked building or vehicle; theft from an unlocked vehicle or job site needs the optional Theft cover add-on, according to AMI's tradies page.
pros: Direct online or phone quote, no broker needed
Bundles tools cover and public liability for small trade businesses
Covers employees' tools and belongings up to $5,000
Monthly or annual payment
cons: Tools cover is capped at $10,000 and public liability at $2 million in the bundle
Theft from an unlocked vehicle or job site needs an optional add-on
Sold direct, so there is no broker to advise on cover
vendors.typical_pricing: Online or phone quote; AMI advertises its Tradies Insurance bundle from $19 a week including GST, based on the most common occupations, paid monthly or annually

vendors.name: iPayroll
vendors.tagline: New Zealand cloud payroll and PAYE intermediary service, founded in 2001, priced per pay run
vendors.market_position: iPayroll is a cloud payroll service founded in New Zealand in 2001 by Martin Gleeson, with offices in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and in Melbourne and Sydney. It handles payday filing with Inland Revenue, KiwiSaver deductions and leave, and as a PAYE intermediary it can collect and pay a customer's PAYE for them. iPayroll says it has 12,000 customers across the group and integrates with Xero, MYOB and HR tools.
vendors.nz_specific_note: iPayroll says it registered as a PAYE intermediary with Inland Revenue in 2006; on its Standard plan it collects PAYE each pay run and pays it to IR for you, and it files payday returns. KiwiSaver deductions and leave are handled; ACC levies are not mentioned on its site.
pros: PAYE intermediary service collects and pays PAYE to Inland Revenue for you
Price calculator on the pricing page, charged per pay run
Employee Kiosk and app for payslips, pay history and leave requests
Xero integration since 2006, plus MYOB and HR tool links
cons: Set-up fees may apply and prices exclude GST and bank fees
DIY-PAYE and Enterprise prices are only by request
No free trial mentioned on the pricing page
ACC levy handling not mentioned
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD per pay run, excluding GST and bank fees: Standard plan priced by people paid and pay frequency via the pricing calculator (shows $13.70 per pay run at its starting setting); set-up fees may apply; DIY-PAYE, Charity and Enterprise pricing on request

vendors.name: Smartly
vendors.tagline: New Zealand payroll software, formerly SmartPayroll, with self-run and Smartly-run payroll plans
vendors.market_position: Smartly, formerly SmartPayroll, is New Zealand payroll software that pays employees into their bank accounts, deducts PAYE, KiwiSaver and other deductions, and files returns with Inland Revenue. It sells self-managed payroll plans, optionally with people management tools, and Smartly-run plans where its team runs the payroll.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Built for New Zealand payroll: PAYE and KiwiSaver deductions and filing with Inland Revenue. Pricing is per employee per pay run plus a monthly platform fee, excluding GST.
pros: Handles PAYE, KiwiSaver deductions and Inland Revenue filing
Choice of running payroll yourself or having Smartly run it
Optional people management tools on top of payroll
cons: A monthly platform fee applies on top of per-employee charges
Prices exclude GST
Charges apply per employee on every pay run, so weekly pay cycles cost more than monthly ones
vendors.typical_pricing: Published by Smartly (indicative, excluding GST): Payroll $2.60 per employee per pay run plus a $51.50 monthly platform fee; Payroll + People Management adds $10 per employee a month; Smartly-run Payroll $6.20 per employee per pay run, from $365 a month minimum. Banking transaction fees may apply.

vendors.name: EWRB (Electrical Workers Registration Board)
vendors.tagline: New Zealand's registration and licensing board for electrical workers, under the Electricity Act 1992
vendors.market_position: The Electrical Workers Registration Board (EWRB) registers and licenses New Zealand electrical workers under the Electricity Act 1992, with MBIE running its portal and public register. Only registered and licensed workers can carry out or supervise prescribed electrical work, and a practising licence must be renewed every 2 years after a Board-approved competence programme. A new registration framework took effect on 1 September 2024, and endorsed classes for high-risk work apply from 1 September 2026.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Registration and a current practising licence are separate: register once in a class such as Electrician, Electrical Installer or Electrical Service Technician, then renew the practising licence every 2 years. Customers can check a worker's licence on the Electrical Workers Public Register. EWRB says it can investigate and prosecute unlicensed prescribed electrical work.
pros: Clear legal route to doing prescribed electrical work in New Zealand
Public register lets customers check a worker's licence
Step-up pathways from Service Technician to Installer and Installer to Electrician
TTMRA pathway for Australian electrical workers
cons: Practising licence must be renewed every 2 years with a competence programme
Individual fees are only shown in the MBIE portal, not on public pages
High-risk work needs an extra endorsed class from 1 September 2026
Employer Licences cost $1,235 per year of term and suit larger organisations
vendors.typical_pricing: Registration and practising licence fees are charged through the MBIE Electrical Workers portal and are not listed on EWRB's public pages; practising licence renews every 2 years; Employer Licence $1,235 per year of the licence term plus certification costs

vendors.name: PGDB (Plumbers, Gasfitters and Drainlayers Board)
vendors.tagline: New Zealand's registration and licensing board for plumbers, gasfitters and drainlayers
vendors.market_position: The Plumbers, Gasfitters and Drainlayers Board (PGDB) registers and licenses plumbers, gasfitters and drainlayers in New Zealand under the Plumbers, Gasfitters, and Drainlayers Act 2006, sets minimum competence standards, and handles complaints, discipline and court prosecutions of people doing unauthorised work. The Board says it is a not-for-profit body funded by fees, with ten ministerially appointed members representing the trade and the public. Registration classes include certifying, plumber, gasfitter or drainlayer, and restricted, plus limited certificates for trainees.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Customers can check a tradesperson's licence on the PGDB public register, and practitioners can show their licence in the PGDB app or on a physical card. Homeowners may only do limited DIY work, such as replacing taps or clearing a blocked drain without altering pipes. From 7 September 2026, certifying plumbers and drainlayers with a self-certification endorsement can sign off their own consented work instead of an inspection by the building consent authority.
pros: Public register lets customers check a tradesperson's licence
Published fees: $100 annual licence plus a $275 levy, incl GST
One board covers plumbing, gasfitting and drainlaying
Self-certification endorsement from September 2026 lets endorsed certifying practitioners sign off their own work
cons: The $275 disciplinary and prosecution levy is paid every year on top of the licence
Renewal each year requires completed CPD
Board exams cost $330 each ($410 for certifying)
Self-certification endorsement costs $2,260 for 3 years
vendors.typical_pricing: Official PGDB fees from 1 April 2026, incl GST: registration $350; annual practising licence $100 per licence; disciplinary and prosecution levy $275 per person per year (one licence $375, two $475, three $575 a year in total); first registration $725 in total; trade exam $330; certifying exam $410; self-certification endorsement $2,260 for 3 years

vendors.name: NoCowboys
vendors.tagline: New Zealand ratings site for tradespeople and businesses, with a $999 a year business registration
vendors.market_position: NoCowboys is a New Zealand ratings and review site for tradespeople and other businesses, run by NoCowboys Limited in Auckland. Consumers search by business type and location, read ratings, contact businesses directly, and can post jobs on a free jobs board for businesses to quote on. NoCowboys says it shows 146,730 ratings (September 2026) and that it takes no commission on jobs.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Covers all of New Zealand. Any consumer can add a business by name and phone number and rate it, so unregistered businesses also collect ratings; paid registration adds a full profile, review tools, a website build and priority over unregistered listings in many areas. NoCowboys says it checks ratings with email verification, IP tracking and requests for quotes or invoices from suspicious raters.
pros: Published price: $999 a year, with no commissions or pay-per-click
Registration includes a profile, replies to reviews, a free website build and domain, and an account manager
Rating checks include email verification, IP tracking and requests for proof of the job
Consumers contact businesses directly, and a free jobs board lets them request quotes
cons: Anyone can add your business and rate it, registered or not
Fees are not refundable except at NoCowboys' discretion
The site does not say whether the $999 includes GST
NoCowboys says most consumers search and contact businesses directly rather than post jobs, so leads depend on your profile
vendors.typical_pricing: Business registration $999 per year (NZD; GST treatment not stated); no commissions and no pay-per-click; no other plans published

vendors.name: PayHero
vendors.tagline: New Zealand payroll software from Wellington's FlexiTime, with automated payday filing and GPS timesheets for trades
vendors.market_position: PayHero is New Zealand payroll software from FlexiTime, a Wellington company that says it has run payroll for Kiwi businesses since 2008 and launched PayHero in 2019. It covers pay runs, automated payday filing with Inland Revenue, leave, and timesheets and leave requests through an employee app. Its trades page adds GPS time tracking, job-level timesheets, tool allowances and mileage reimbursements.
vendors.nz_specific_note: PayHero says it handles leave in line with the Holidays Act 2003 and current government guidance, and calculates public holiday entitlements from work patterns and timesheet history. The Employment Leave Act 2026 replaces the Holidays Act from 6 August 2028; PayHero has said it plans to update the software and move existing leave balances across before then.
pros: Published NZD prices, pay as you go with no lock-in contract
Automated payday filing of PAYE with Inland Revenue
Trades features: GPS time tracking, job-level timesheets, tool allowances and mileage reimbursements
Public holiday entitlements calculated from work patterns and timesheet history
14-day free trial with no credit card
cons: Origin plan is capped at 10 employees
Base fee plus a per-employee charge each month, excluding GST
GPS clock-in, timesheet approvals and break calculations need Super or above
Leave rules change when the Employment Leave Act 2026 starts in August 2028
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD excl GST, per month: Origin $24 base + $4 per employee (up to 10 employees); Super $39 base + $6 per employee; Universe $59 base + $7 per employee; charged only for employees with pay or timesheet activity, billed monthly in arrears; 14-day free trial; enterprise pricing on request

vendors.name: LBP (Licensed Building Practitioners)
vendors.tagline: New Zealand licensing scheme for builders and designers who do or supervise Restricted Building Work on homes
vendors.market_position: The Licensed Building Practitioners (LBP) scheme licenses people assessed as competent to carry out building work essential to the structure or weathertightness of residential buildings. It started in November 2007 under the Building Act 2004 and is overseen by the Building Practitioners Board, part of MBIE. Licence classes are Design 1-3, Site 1-3, Carpentry, Roofing, External Plastering, Brick and Blocklaying, and Foundations.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Restricted Building Work (consented work on a home's primary structure, weathertightness or certain fire safety design) must be done or supervised by an LBP, and breaches can bring an instant fine or a court fine of up to $50,000. Homeowners can check a practitioner on the public LBP register, and LBPs must relicense every year and keep up skills maintenance.
pros: Required to do or supervise Restricted Building Work on homes
Public register lets homeowners check a practitioner
Published application and assessment fees, including GST
Classes cover design, site, carpentry, roofing, plastering, masonry and foundations
cons: Relicensing every year plus ongoing skills maintenance
Several classes and areas of practice to choose from
Only Restricted Building Work needs an LBP, not all building work
Applicants may need a face-to-face interview, at extra cost, if the written application falls short
vendors.typical_pricing: Official fees, incl GST: application fee $250 plus an assessment fee per class, for example $281.11 for Carpentry, Site 1, Roofing, External Plastering, Brick and Blocklaying or Foundations (one area of practice), $776.89-$1,012.00 for Design 1-3; streamlined assessments from $127.78 where available; licences are renewed every year (renewal fee not shown on the pages read)

vendors.name: ServiceM8 (NZ)
vendors.tagline: Australian-made job management app for small trade and service businesses, priced in NZD by jobs per month with unlimited users
vendors.market_position: ServiceM8 is job management software from ServiceM8 Pty Ltd, an Australian company, built around its iPhone and iPad app, with ServiceM8 Lite for Android field staff. Its New Zealand site lists NZD prices per business by jobs per month, and every paid plan includes unlimited users. ServiceM8 says contractors around the world have used it to manage over $50 billion in jobs, and that it won Xero's Global Innovation App of the Year award.
vendors.nz_specific_note: ServiceM8 runs a New Zealand site with NZD prices and offers help through local partners; its terms are with the Australian company under Australian law. It shows Xero Preferred App and MYOB Certified Add-on badges and also integrates with QuickBooks Online. The NZ pricing page does not say whether prices include GST.
pros: Published NZD prices, from a free plan up to $349 a month
Unlimited users on every paid plan
No lock-in, and the 14-day trial needs no payment details
Integrates with Xero, MYOB and QuickBooks Online
cons: Optimised for iPhone and iPad; Android users get ServiceM8 Lite
Price rises with monthly job volume, and the Free plan is limited to 1 user and 30 jobs
Card processing costs 1.19% + 30c to 3.10% + 30c depending on plan
Terms are under Australian law, and the NZ pricing page does not state GST treatment
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD per business per month (GST treatment not stated): Free $0 (1 user, 30 jobs), Starter $29 (50 jobs), Growing $79 (150 jobs), Premium $149 (500 jobs), Premium Plus $349 (1,500 jobs, then 20c per job); unlimited users on paid plans; extra SMS 10c; 14-day free trial

vendors.name: Simpro (NZ)
vendors.tagline: Job, project and service management software for trade contractors, from Simpro Group, with an Auckland office
vendors.market_position: Simpro is job, project and service management software for trade contractors, covering quotes, scheduling, dispatch, invoicing, payments and inventory. It started in Brisbane and is now run by Simpro Group, which raised US$350 million from K1 in November 2021 and also owns AroFlo, ClockShark and BigChange. Simpro says more than 8,500 service, project and maintenance businesses use it.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Simpro lists a New Zealand office on Albert Street in central Auckland with an 0800 number. It is a Platinum Partner of Master Plumbers New Zealand, and its Xero NZ app syncs contacts, invoices, supplier invoices, payments, timesheets and inventory journals.
pros: Quoting, scheduling, dispatch, invoicing, payments and inventory in one system
Auckland office and a New Zealand 0800 number
Platinum Partner of Master Plumbers New Zealand
Two-way Xero sync, listed on the Xero NZ app store
cons: No public prices: you need a sales quote
Initial setup fee for onboarding, training and data migration
Add-ons such as fleet tracking and maintenance planning change the price
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Simpro says pricing depends on team size (office and field users) and add-ons, plus an initial setup fee

vendors.name: AroFlo (NZ)
vendors.tagline: Melbourne-based job management software for Australian and New Zealand trades, part of Simpro Group, with an NZ 0800 line
vendors.market_position: AroFlo is job management software for trade businesses in Australia and New Zealand, founded by an Australian electrician and headquartered in Melbourne. Simpro bought AroFlo in November 2021, and it is now part of Simpro Group, which also owns Simpro, BigChange and ClockShark. AroFlo says more than 2,800 businesses use it, and it has added an AI layer called AroFlo Lightning.
vendors.nz_specific_note: AroFlo has a New Zealand support line (0800 853 992) but no separate NZ pricing or NZ site section. Its supplier integrations include New Zealand wholesalers Plumbing World and Ideal Electrical NZ, and it links to Xero, MYOB, QuickBooks and Reckon for accounting.
pros: Published starting price: $80 per user a month, falling as users are added
Supplier integrations with NZ wholesalers Plumbing World and Ideal Electrical NZ
Accounting links to Xero, MYOB, QuickBooks and Reckon
New Zealand 0800 support line
cons: Minimum of 3 users, so a sole trader pays for at least 3 licences
Setup fee on top of the subscription
Pricing page does not state currency or GST, and there is no NZ price list
GPS tracking and the AI bill scanner are paid add-ons
vendors.typical_pricing: From $80 per user/month (currency and GST not stated; no separate NZ price), minimum 3 users; per-user rate falls as users are added; setup fee applies

vendors.name: Invven
vendors.tagline: New Zealand-built invoicing, quoting and inventory software for trade businesses, with cost prices hidden from customer documents
vendors.market_position: Invven is invoicing, quoting, job and inventory software from INVVEN Ltd, a New Zealand company. Its founder, Shane Smale, says on the About page that he owned and ran a New Zealand motorhome dealership for 27 years. Invven's inventory tools include barcode scanning, low-stock alerts and what it calls Stealth Margins, which keep cost prices off customer documents, and its AI tools turn photos into quotes and voice notes into invoices. It is a young product: its terms took effect on 1 May 2026.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Terms are with INVVEN Ltd under New Zealand law, and all billing is in NZD. Prices exclude GST, and 15% GST is added at checkout for NZ customers. The site can show approximate prices in AUD, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD or ZAR, but billing is still in NZD.
pros: Published NZD prices from $29 a month, with annual plans priced at 10 months
14-day free trial with no payment details
Inventory built in: barcode scanning, low-stock alerts and cost prices hidden from customer documents
AI photo-to-quote and voice-to-invoice tools on Professional and Business
Xero and MYOB two-way sync on the Business plan
cons: Young product: its terms took effect on 1 May 2026
AI Receptionist costs extra, sold as prepaid minute packs from $39 NZD+GST for 60 minutes
WhatsApp messages cost $0.05 each on Professional and Business
Starter is limited to 1 user and 50 customers; GPS jobs and Xero/MYOB sync need Business
Subscription fees are non-refundable (annual plans after 14 days from payment)
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD excl GST (15% GST added for NZ customers), per month: Starter $29 (1 user, up to 50 customers), Professional $79 (3 users, unlimited customers, Photo to Quote and Voice to Invoice), Business $159 (unlimited users, GPS job management, Xero/MYOB sync, API); annual plans priced at 10 months; 14-day free trial, no card. Add-ons: AI Receptionist minute packs from $39 for 60 minutes; WhatsApp $0.05 per message

vendors.name: Trade Me Services
vendors.tagline: Services section of Trade Me, where providers pay $89 to list for 90 days and customers browse by category
vendors.market_position: Trade Me Services is the services section of Trade Me, the New Zealand online marketplace owned by private equity firm Apax Partners, which was reported in February 2026 to be seeking a buyer. Providers list a service under categories such as trades, domestic services, events and health, and customers browse the listings. On 30 September 2026 the Trades category showed 732 listings, including 280 in building and construction, 39 in electrical and gas, and 16 in plumbing.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Trade Me's help centre lists a $89 fee for a 90-day Services listing, with optional Feature ($189) and Super Feature ($209) upgrades and no other promotional extras; extending or relisting charges the fees again. On 30 September 2026 the web listing page showed a system-upgrade notice asking providers to list through the app or desktop site.
pros: Sits inside Trade Me, alongside its Marketplace, Motors and Property sections
Published fee: $89 for a 90-day listing
Trade categories cover building, electrical and gas, plumbing, roofing, painting and more
Low competition in some trades: 16 plumbing listings on 30 September 2026
cons: General services directory: trades sit alongside domestic, events and health services
Fees are charged again every 90 days when a listing is extended or relisted
Featured placement costs $189 or $209 on top of the listing fee
The fees are on Trade Me's help pages, not the Services pages
vendors.typical_pricing: $89 per Services listing for 90 days; optional Feature ($189) or Super Feature ($209) upgrade; fees are charged again on each extension or relist, with an optional auto-extend every 90 days

vendors.name: Localist
vendors.tagline: New Zealand business directory built from the Companies register, where owners pay from $5 a month to claim and verify their profile
vendors.market_position: Localist is a New Zealand business directory that New Zealand Post launched in 2010 as an Auckland print directory and sold in 2014 to a management group led by CEO Christina Domecq. It now lists businesses from the Companies register (933,761 on its homepage in September 2026) and sells monthly plans that let owners claim, verify and expand their profile for Google, Maps and AI assistants. Its plans include a contact form but do not mention leads, quote requests or job requests.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Profiles are tied to the NZBN and the Companies Office register, and the Verified plan adds an NZBN-verified badge. Prices include GST and are billed monthly in NZD in advance; cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period, with no refunds for partial periods.
pros: Published prices including GST, from $5 a month
Many businesses are already listed from the Companies register, ready to claim
NZBN-verified badge on Verified and above
Monthly billing, cancel at the end of any billing period
cons: No free plan for owners to manage their profile
No leads, quote requests or job requests in any plan
Review monitoring and AI support only on the $149 Growth plan
No refunds for partial billing periods
vendors.typical_pricing: NZD per month including GST: Claim $5, Verified $29, Visible $49, Authority $89, Growth $149; billed monthly in advance; spring offer of 25% off any plan for 12 months (Claim $3.75 to Growth $111.75) at 30 September 2026

vendors.name: FairTrades NZ
vendors.tagline: NZ quote marketplace: homeowners post jobs free, tradies quote with no lead fees or commission
vendors.market_position: FairTrades is a New Zealand job marketplace where homeowners post a job free, compare quotes side by side and share contact details only after accepting a quote. Tradies build a profile and must pass FairTrades' minimum provider review before quoting; FairTrades says it charges no lead fees and no success commission, and earns from tradie plans instead. Its site lists 28 trades in four groups, and the 6 recent jobs it showed on 30 September 2026 were all in Christchurch.
vendors.nz_specific_note: FairTrades calls itself Kiwi owned and operated, but its site, terms and privacy policy do not name the company behind it. Its terms say the provider review does not mean every licence, qualification or insurance policy has been checked. The recent jobs shown were all in Christchurch, so check demand in your area before paying for a plan.
pros: No lead fees and 0% success commission on every plan
Free plan allows up to 3 quotes per rolling 30 days once verified
Paid plans do not auto-renew
Pro and Business include JobLedger for jobs, reminders and invoices
cons: Operating company not named on the site, terms or privacy policy
Recent jobs shown on the site were all in Christchurch
More than 3 quotes per 30 days needs a paid plan
Plans page does not say whether prices include GST
vendors.typical_pricing: Tradies: Free $0 (up to 3 quotes per rolling 30 days); Pro $50 per 30 days; Business $95 per 30 days with 2 tradie seats, extra tradies $45 each. No lead fees or success commission, no auto-renewal; GST treatment not stated. Free for homeowners

vendors.name: Builtin
vendors.tagline: Tauranga-based insurance broker for builders and trades, with roots in 2002
vendors.market_position: Builtin Insurance Brokers Limited is a Tauranga-based broker for builders and trade businesses, holding a Class 2 financial advice provider licence (FSP28581) and belonging to the Steadfast broker network. It traces its history to 2002, when it began insuring Certified Builders Association members, and says it is family-owned, with Keryl and Ben Rickard as shareholders and directors. It places cover with insurers including Ando, IAG, Vero, QBE, Lloyd's, DUAL, UANZ and AIG, across liability, contract works, tools, commercial vehicles, professional indemnity, bonds and a Residential Completion Guarantee.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Builtin offers LBP professional indemnity for Licensed Building Practitioners (errors in records of work and negligent supervision) and instant online quotes for liability, tools and vehicles. Its Residential Completion Guarantee covers a homeowner's lost deposit and non-completion up to 10% of the contract value, to a maximum of $100,000, with no post-completion defects cover. It is the named insurance partner for TANZ, NZCCA, Building Hub and PlaceMakers Plus members.
pros: Broker specialising in construction and trades, with its own FAP licence
LBP professional indemnity for Licensed Building Practitioners
Instant online quotes for liability, tools and vehicles
Residential Completion Guarantee you can offer homeowners
Member deals through TANZ, NZCCA, Building Hub and PlaceMakers Plus
cons: No published prices; premiums quoted per business
Paid by insurer commission and may add advisory fees
Completion Guarantee has no post-completion defects cover
Steadfast network takes up to 1.5% of each policy from insurers
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Instant online quotes for liability, tools and vehicles; Builtin is paid by insurer commission and may charge advisory fees

vendors.name: BizCover (NZ)
vendors.tagline: Online business insurance for NZ tradies, with cover from AIG, Ando, DUAL and BHSI
vendors.market_position: BizCover is an online business insurance platform, trading in New Zealand as BizCover Limited, that sells cover from four insurers (AIG, Ando, DUAL New Zealand and Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance) and acts as the insurer's agent, not the customer's. It was founded in Sydney in 2008, is listed as one of AUB Group's business areas, and its NZ homepage says more than 18,000 NZ small businesses use it. It says it covers 900+ occupations, including builders, plumbers, electricians, painters and other trades.
vendors.nz_specific_note: For tradies BizCover sells public liability at six limits from $1M to $20M, tool and portable equipment cover, professional indemnity and other covers online, with policy documents emailed on purchase. On its tradie page it gives expected averages of $32 a month for public liability and $80 a month for tool cover (July 2023 to June 2024 customer average, a guide only). It adds a fee of $20 to $150 + GST per policy and keeps its commission and fees if you cancel.
pros: Quote and buy online, with policy documents emailed straight away
Public liability limits from $1M to $20M
Publishes average monthly costs as a guide
Pay monthly or annually
Full refund if you call within 14 days of an unwanted auto-renewal
cons: Acts as the insurer's agent, not yours
BizCover fee of $20-$150 + GST per policy on top of the premium
Paying monthly adds $8 + GST a month
Commission and fees kept if you cancel
Policies renew automatically unless you contact BizCover
vendors.typical_pricing: Premium quoted per business; BizCover's tradie page gives expected averages of $32/month for public liability and $80/month for tool cover (July 2023-June 2024 customer average, guide only). Plus a BizCover fee of $20-$150 + GST per policy, and $8 + GST/month if paying by instalments

vendors.name: Thankyou Payroll
vendors.tagline: NZ payroll that files and pays PAYE to IRD for you, free for registered charities
vendors.market_position: Thankyou Payroll is a New Zealand cloud payroll service founded in Dunedin in 2009 and now based in Wellington; it says it is owned by Generous Ventures, which grew out of the Thankyou Charitable Trust, and puts its profits back into communities. It says it is an IRD-accredited PAYE intermediary: employers transfer the gross payroll to Thankyou, which pays staff, files payday information and pays deductions to IRD. It says over 7,000 organisations use it. RNZ reported on 10 September 2026 that Thankyou Payroll was caught up in a global breach of the Metabase reporting tool that exposed names, IRD numbers, addresses, bank account details and payment histories.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Thankyou Payroll says it files payday information and pays PAYE, KiwiSaver, student loan and child support deductions to IRD for you on every plan. It calculates ordinary and average weekly pay and relevant and average daily pay for Holidays Act leave, tracks annual and sick leave balances, and posts pay journals to Xero.
pros: PAYE intermediary service (payday filing and IRD payments) on every plan
Published prices with a monthly cap; you pay only for pays you run
No setup fee or contract, and nothing to pay until your first pay
Free for registered charities
Xero journals, configurable timesheets and an employee app
cons: Per-pay fee makes weekly pay runs cost more, up to the monthly cap
Gross payroll must reach Thankyou before payday (2 days ahead on the 2 Day plan)
Hit by a September 2026 data breach via the Metabase reporting tool, per RNZ
vendors.typical_pricing: 2 Day plan: $6 per pay + $2 per employee; Fast plan (overnight processing): $6 per pay + $2.50 per employee; + GST. Monthly caps excl. GST: $44 (1-3 employees), $79 (4-10), $159 (11-30), $259 (31-50), $399 (51+). No setup fee or contract; free until first pay; $0 for registered charities

vendors.name: Crystal Payroll
vendors.tagline: Auckland-made cloud payroll with automatic IRD payday filing, running since 2005
vendors.market_position: Crystal Payroll is a New Zealand cloud payroll and timesheet service based in Birkenhead, Auckland, which says it has been running since 2005 and serves thousands of Kiwi businesses. It says it is an IRD-accredited PAYE intermediary and files payday returns to IRD for you two working days after payday, from a Payday Filing Dashboard. It handles KiwiSaver and holiday pay calculations, including for variable-rate and shift workers, and connects to Xero, MYOB, Reckon and Farm Focus.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Crystal Payroll says it is an IRD-accredited PAYE intermediary and files payday returns automatically two working days after the pay date. It says it manages holiday pay and leave calculations under New Zealand law, including for staff on variable rates and shift workers, and employees can submit timesheets and leave requests through its app.
pros: Automatic IRD payday filing from a Payday Filing Dashboard
Holiday pay and leave calculations for variable-rate and shift workers
Employee app for timesheets and leave requests
No minimum period, and money back within 30 days of your first pay run, Crystal says
Connects to Xero, MYOB, Reckon and Farm Focus
cons: Published price covers up to 5 employees; bigger teams use a calculator or ask sales
One-off $50 registration fee, and training costs $60 an hour
Data migration priced on request
vendors.typical_pricing: From $19.90/month for up to 5 employees, excl. GST; other headcounts priced by the site's cost calculator (contact sales above 500 employees). One-off $50 registration fee; optional training $60/hour; data migration quoted

vendors.name: WorkSafe New Zealand
vendors.tagline: NZ's work health and safety regulator: HSWA duties apply to every trade business
vendors.market_position: WorkSafe New Zealand is a Crown agency and, in its own words, New Zealand's primary work health and safety regulator under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA); it also administers the Gas Act 1992 and Electricity Act 1992. HSWA duties apply by law to every PCBU, including self-employed tradies, and WorkSafe enforces them through workplace assessments, formal warnings, enforceable undertakings and prosecutions. Construction is one of its listed priority industries.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Trade businesses must give WorkSafe 24 hours' notice of particularly hazardous work, such as construction or scaffolding with a risk of falling 5 metres or more, or trenches over 1.5 metres deep that are deeper than they are wide. HSWA amendments take effect on 1 April 2027, bringing in small and large PCBU categories and a focus on critical risks; WorkSafe published its first guidance on them in September 2026.
pros: Guidance and tools on WorkSafe's site, including new guides for the 2027 changes
Online notification of hazardous work and incidents
Public registers to check asbestos licence holders and gas practitioners
Meeting HSWA duties reduces the risk of enforcement action
cons: Duties apply by law; there is no opt-out
24 hours' notice needed before particularly hazardous work
Law changes on 1 April 2027 mean reviewing how you manage critical risks
Compliance is a baseline, not a badge to market
vendors.typical_pricing: No registration or membership fee: HSWA duties apply to every PCBU by law. Some work needs a separate WorkSafe licence or permit, such as asbestos removal

vendors.name: Registered Master Builders Association
vendors.tagline: Voluntary builders' association whose members can offer the Master Build 10-Year Guarantee
vendors.market_position: The Registered Master Builders Association of New Zealand Incorporated is a voluntary membership body for residential and commercial building companies, with 23 branches and six regional hubs. Members get standard building contracts, expert advice, free dispute resolution for themselves and their clients, discount schemes, entry to the members-only House of the Year awards and access to the Master Build 10-Year Guarantee, which the association offers through its wholly owned Master Build Services Limited. Membership is not a licence: licensing for structural and weathertightness work on homes sits with the government-run LBP scheme.
vendors.nz_specific_note: The 10-Year Guarantee covers a homeowner's lost deposit (up to $50,000 or 10% of the contract), non-completion (up to $500,000 or 20%), materials and workmanship for 2 years after practical completion and structural defects for 10 years, up to $1,000,000 or the contract value in total. It is available only through a Master Builders member, with fees of $730 (partial cover) to $6,325 (full cover) incl. GST for contracts of $30,000 to $4 million; it is not available for contracts over $4 million.
pros: Members can offer homeowners the Master Build 10-Year Guarantee
Standard building contracts and expert legal, employment and H&S advice
Free dispute resolution for members and their clients
Members-only House of the Year awards and a find-a-builder listing
Fees published in full, from $260 + GST a year for contractors
cons: Residential builders pay $1,605-$3,475 + GST a year (2026), by turnover
Fees rise in 2027, for example to $1,670-$3,615 for residential builders
Voluntary: it does not replace LBP licensing
Guarantee fee of $730-$6,325 incl. GST per project
vendors.typical_pricing: Annual fees 2026 (2027), excl. GST: Contractor $260 ($270); Residential Builder by turnover $1,605-$3,475 ($1,670-$3,615); Volume and Commercial Builder $4,160 ($4,330); Major Contractor $8,810 ($9,170); Individual $135 ($140); apprentices free for member employees. 10-Year Guarantee per project: $730-$5,500 partial or $910-$6,325 full cover incl. GST, for contracts of $30,000-$4M (no cover above $4M)

vendors.name: Master Plumbers, Gasfitters & Drainlayers NZ
vendors.tagline: Voluntary membership body for plumbers, gasfitters and drainlayers, with a homeowner guarantee
vendors.market_position: Master Plumbers, Gasfitters and Drainlayers NZ Inc. is a voluntary membership body for the three trades that says it has operated since 1901 and has 19 branches. Business membership is open to certifying plumbers, gasfitters or drainlayers who have run their own business for at least six months, or businesses employing certified tradespeople. Members get a free technical helpline, employment and legal helpline support, a health and safety manual, training, and discounts on fuel cards and Site Safe membership; it also runs Masterlink, a group apprenticeship scheme.
vendors.nz_specific_note: Homeowners who use a member are covered by the 12-month residential Master Plumbers Guarantee of up to $20,000 incl. GST, for substandard workmanship and prepaid money lost if the member goes into liquidation or bankruptcy; complaints must be lodged within 12 months of the invoice. Membership is voluntary: registration and licensing for restricted plumbing, gasfitting and drainlaying work sits with the PGDB.
pros: Members' residential work is backed by a 12-month guarantee of up to $20,000 incl. GST
Free technical helpline for plumbing, gasfitting and drainlaying
Employment advice and 20 free minutes on a legal helpline
10% off Site Safe membership, plus fuel and first aid discounts
Fees published by staff size, payable monthly or yearly
cons: Business fees of $1,241-$2,685 a year incl. GST, plus a $175 + GST application fee
Voluntary: does not replace PGDB registration and licensing
Business membership needs a certifying tradesperson and 6+ months in business
Guarantee capped at $20,000 per member for liquidation or bankruptcy claims
vendors.typical_pricing: Business membership incl. GST: $103/month or $1,241/year (one person) up to $224/month or $2,685/year (100+ staff), plus a one-off $175 + GST application fee. Apprentice $40 + GST/year (waived for Masterlink apprentices); Retired $80 + GST/year
